blocks.heading: Research Questions
blocks.text: The proposed mechanism replacement targets two operational questions. First, what exact mathematical relaxation conditions permit static equilibrium axioms of dense matter equations of state to support masses beyond the static Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit without violating the causality bound? Second, what numerical or analytical techniques verify the predicted mass-spin relation that distinguishes massive millisecond pulsars from isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down systems? These questions are delimited by unresolved design dependencies requiring human confirmation.

blocks.heading: Planned Contributions
blocks.text: This research plan contributes a candidate mechanism unifying isolated spin-down and binary recycling via relaxed equation of state axioms. It formalizes the relation between gravitational mass and spin period for massive neutron stars exceeding the static limit. The contribution relies on binary mass accretion and angular momentum transfer modeled as a continuous thermodynamic and mechanical perturbation, distinguishing evolutionary channels through derived model outputs.

blocks.heading: Design Assumptions and Scope
blocks.text: The design assumes that companion ablation primarily affects the surface and magnetosphere, allowing the core mass-spin relation to remain governed by the relaxed effective equilibrium axioms. The scope is strictly bounded by the causality constraint and the requirement that standard rotational support models do not fully explain the observed population of massive millisecond pulsars without relaxing the static axioms.

blocks.heading: Transition to Formalization
blocks.text: The formalization of these questions and contributions is deferred to the definitions and propositions ledger, which owns the complete definition of the relaxed axioms and the candidate theorem entry.
